cases.reason: The inclusive emergency definition covers a repair problem needing immediate remediation to prevent likely serious damage; the candidate preserves the nonexclusive scope.
The source says includes but is not limited to, so only improperly closes the definition.
The definition expressly lists weeding, mowing and pruning as nonexclusive examples.
The list identifies included activities; it does not require every listed activity on every visit.
The definition expressly excludes security deposits and fees from rent.
The candidate reverses the express exclusion of security deposits and fees.
The definition expressly includes the agent or successor in interest of the listed landlord roles.
The candidate reverses the express inclusion of agents and successors.
The public-sale statement in the notice is an express condition of subdivision (b).
The selected passage conditions release on a public-sale notice, not notice of personal retention by the landlord.
The opening clause expressly requires that property was not released pursuant to subdivision (a).
The candidate reverses the express not-released condition.
Reclamation by the former tenant is one expressly stated alternative in the reclaimant condition, not a sufficient condition for the entire release duty.
The alternative other reclaimant must reasonably be believed by the landlord to own the property; the candidate expressly lacks that condition.
The passage also permits reclamation by another person reasonably believed by the landlord to be its owner, so personal reclamation by the former tenant is not necessary in every case.
The source connects former tenant and reasonably-believed other owner by or; either satisfies the claimant component while other conditions remain necessary.
